title: Reorder roadmap so acceleration work comes first, study alongside
summary: Edit docs/design/roadmap.md so a new first acceleration step (sccache hit rate, parallel jobs with shared CHANGELOG/decisions collisions, native PR landing, timings fed back) precedes the others, citing the BRIEF.md 2026-10-13 "Athena owns acceleration" addendum. The firstmate study step (RM-6) is marked as running alongside it. Docs only, no code.

defaults_applied.how: The reordered roadmap explains the reason for the order to an outside reader.
The new step cites BRIEF.md line numbers and labels the 0-hit sccache figure as user-reported, not measured.
Docs-only reorder; no implementation of the speed work.
Recovered the step content from roadmap.md RM-8, AD-11 and decisions D79-D81.

assumptions: The 'acceleration' addendum is BRIEF.md 'Athena owns acceleration' dated 2026-10-13 (lines 494-496); BRIEF.md itself is not edited.
The sccache '0 hits' figure comes from the user, not from anything measured in the repository; the roadmap will cite it as reported by the user.
Existing RM-n identifiers stay stable where possible to avoid breaking references; a new step is added at the top and RM-8 and AD-11 rows move into it.
Nothing is implemented by this change; the roadmap remains a proposal, as it states.

acceptance_criteria.text: docs/design/roadmap.md opens its ordered steps with an acceleration step that cites the BRIEF.md 2026-10-13 'Athena owns acceleration' addendum (BRIEF.md:494-496).

The acceleration step covers: sccache showing 0 cache hits (diagnose and fix), parallel jobs including collisions on shared CHANGELOG.md and docs/decisions.md, native pull-request landing, and timings fed back into the system; each with a 'done when' test.
The firstmate study step (formerly RM-6) is stated to run alongside the acceleration step, not after it, and the 'How the order was chosen' paragraph is rewritten to explain the new order.

Every partial or uncovered row still appears in exactly one step; rows moved from RM-8 (A4-3, A5-3, A5-4, A5-5, SD-6, AD-4, AD-5, AD-9) and AD-11 are not duplicated, and the stated step count and row total are correct.
Any references to step numbers or 'first three steps' in strategy-view.md, requirements-map.md and README.md are consistent with the new order; CHANGELOG.md has an entry for the reorder.
Run `git diff --stat` and `git status` to confirm only documentation files changed; run `cargo test` to confirm nothing else broke.

out_of_scope: Implementing any acceleration work (sccache fix, parallel jobs, PR landing, timing feedback).
Running or changing the firstmate study.
departures: Docs-only edit is cheaper than the reference median; counts and cross-references add some verification risk.
